newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply higher, as December Standard & Poor's 500s' performance in record high territory once again reminded traders and analysts of the strength of the market's bull trend.
"We are having a market melt-up," said Jack Bouroudjian, vice president of equity derivatives at Credit Agricole.

December S&Ps gained 9.80 points to set a contract high at 707.50 late in the day after rallying above the 706.00 level and a daily trendline area of 704.00 and 705.00 amid swaths of commission house and dealer buying. December is seen testing 710.00 and the 711.25 in the very near term, traders said.

"We've come to our senses," Bouroudjian said. "Growth is not a reason to raise rates. People are now convinced that rates are going lower, which means this market is going up, up, up -- you can underline it."
September nonfarm payrolls fell 40,000, versus the average trade estimate of up 166,000 and against August's downward revised increase of 241,000, while the unemployment rate rose to 5.2 percent.
"The numbers really set the stage for the rally," one trader said.
December S&Ps rose tentatively at the start of pit trade, despite rising sharply on GLOBEX, but buying and short-covering gained momentum and pushed December above the 702.50 level by mid-morning.
One trader said arbitrage buy programs were touched off at a premium of 6.00 points to the cash S&P market. Fair value was at 5.09 points, traders said.

"I'm bullish on America," one S&P futures floor trader said, adding that the Dow Jones Transportation Average was rising in sync with the Dow Industrials. "You have to love this kind of price action."
"The stock market held its ground even when bonds were factoring in a rate hike, and that sent a clear signal that growth is driving this market," Bouroudjian said.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were up 9.50 at 707.20, KBT Value Lines were up 7.05 at 653.50, New Composites were up 4.60 at 377.30, Nikkeis were down 60.0 at 21,240, Midcap 400s were up 2.70 at 248.20, and Nasdaq 100s were 16.85 points higher at 767.25.
